_meta.indication: Pediculocide indicated for the topical treatment of head lice infestation in patients 6 months of age and older

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 pivotal clinical study (one of two pivotal trials)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled study; conducted in 5 centers across the US
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 6 months of age and older with active head lice infestation; primary cohort was the youngest child in a household with at least 3 live lice
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects who were lice free 14 days after the second 10 minute application
pivotal_trials.n: N=63 (benzyl alcohol 5%) vs N=62 (vehicle) in primary cohort ITT
pivotal_trials.result: Lice free: 48/63 (76.2%) with L.A. 5% vs 3/62 (4.8%) vehicle; p < .001

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 pivotal clinical study (one of two pivotal trials)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled study; conducted in 5 centers
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 6 months of age and older with active head lice infestation; primary cohort was the youngest child in a household with at least 3 live lice
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects who were lice free 14 days after the second 10 minute application
pivotal_trials.n: N=64 (benzyl alcohol 5%) vs N=61 (vehicle) in primary cohort ITT
pivotal_trials.result: Lice free: 48/64 (75.0%) with L.A. 5% vs 16/61 (26.2%) vehicle; p < .001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>1% and more common than placebo): ocular irritation, application site irritation, and application site anesthesia and hypoesthesia. Application site irritation 2% (11/478) vs 1% (2/336) vehicle; application site anesthesia & hypoesthesia 2% (10/478) vs 0% vehicle. With onset after treatment: ocular irritation 6% (26/428) vs 1% (3/313) vehicle. No deaths and no serious adverse events were reported.
target_moa: Benzyl alcohol 5% lotion acts by stunning the respiratory spiracles of the louse so they remain open, allowing the lotion to occlude the breathing apparatus and cause asphyxiation and death of the louse

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened and no vote was held: NDA 22-129 was not presented to the Dermatology and Ophthalmology Drugs Advisory Committee because systemic exposure to benzyl alcohol following topical treatment was low and no concerning safety signals were documented

summary.text: NDA 22-129 was a 505(b)(2) application relying on literature references for some nonclinical toxicology information. It received an Approvable action on July 14, 2008, was addressed by a complete response submitted October 17, 2008, and was approved as a full (not accelerated) approval based on two randomized, vehicle-controlled trials. The pediatric study requirement for ages 6 months to 18 years was fulfilled.

citations.quote: “This NDA submission is a 505(b)(2) application because the sponsor is relying on literature references to satisfy some aspects of nonclinical toxicology information needed to support the safety of benzyl alcohol (primarily systemic repeat dose toxicology and genetic toxicology).
This application received an Approvable decision on 07/14/08.
We note that you have fulfilled the pediatric study requirement for ages 6 months to 18 years for this application.

basis.text: First cycle approvable action was issued because of the potential safety issue regarding the elevated and sporadic systemic exposure to benzyl alcohol observed in Study SU-01-2007
